cards.name: Arcane Insight
cards.effect: Arcane Insight. Tags: passive, knowledge. Gain proficiency in Arcana, or expertise if already proficient. After examining a magical item, spell residue, ward or active magical effect for 1 minute, you may make an Intelligence (Arcana) check to identify its school, broad function or elemental signature. The Director sets the normal knowledge DC; failure supplies no fabricated information.

source.originalText: Arcane Insight: Identify magical effects and items with greater accuracy than non-mages.

cards.name: Arcane Missile
cards.effect: Arcane Missile. Tags: mage-spell, arcane, damage. The missile automatically hits one creature you can perceive within range and deals S d4 + M force damage. No attack roll or saving throw is made. It is non-elemental, so casting it clears an Elemental Focus Nuke Chain. Multiple missiles are represented by the scaling dice, not separate hits or triggers.

source.originalText: Arcane Missile: Launch bolts of pure arcane energy that unerringly strike your target.

cards.name: Resonance Shield
cards.cost: Spend X RP, where X is 1, 2 or 3
cards.duration: 1 minute or until temporary HP are lost
cards.effect: Resonance Shield. Tags: mage-spell, abjuration, protection. Spend 1-3 RP and gain temporary HP equal to X × (S + M). Temporary HP do not stack. This spell is non-elemental and therefore clears an active Elemental Nuke Chain. Its RP payment cannot be reduced below 1 by Spell Efficiency.

source.originalText: Resonance Shield: Convert a portion of your Resonance Points into a temporary protective barrier.

cards.name: Blink
cards.effect: Blink. Tags: mage-spell, teleportation. Teleport to an unoccupied space you can perceive within 30 feet. This movement does not provoke opportunity attacks and cannot pass through planar wards that prohibit teleportation. Blink deals no damage and is non-elemental, so using it clears an active Elemental Nuke Chain.

source.originalText: Blink: Teleport a short distance to avoid danger or reposition.

cards.name: Elemental Affinity
cards.frequency: Always after Elemental Focus is chosen
cards.effect: Elemental Affinity. Tags: passive, elemental. Gain resistance to the damage type of your current Elemental Focus: fire for Fire, cold for Cold or lightning for Lightning. If Elemental Pivot temporarily changes your Focus, this resistance changes with it and returns to your original element when the Pivot ends.

source.originalText: Elemental Affinity: Gain a minor resistance to your chosen element once selected.

cards.name: Elemental Bolt
cards.effect: Elemental Bolt. Tags: mage-spell, elemental, focus, damage. Make a Mage spell attack. On a hit deal S d8 + M damage of your current Focus. Fire: target takes 1d4 fire at the start of its next turn. Cold: Speed -10 feet until the end of its next turn. Lightning: one different enemy within 10 feet takes S lightning damage. Secondary damage creates no new spell cast or chain credit.

source.originalText: Elemental Bolt: Cast a bolt of your chosen element (once selected) that deals additional effects based on the element.

cards.name: Arcane Stability
cards.effect: Arcane Stability. Tags: arcanist, passive. When damage causes you to make a concentration save for a Mage spell, add +2 to that save. This bonus does not stack with another feature named Arcane Stability and does not change the concentration DC. It does not prevent Silence, incapacitation or effects that end concentration without a save.

source.originalText: Arcane Stability: Reduce spell fizzle chance by 25%.

cards.name: Elemental Surge
cards.effect: Elemental Surge. Tags: mage-spell, arcanist, elemental, focus, damage. Make a Mage spell attack. On a hit deal (S+1)d8 + M damage of your current Focus. Fire also applies the Focus Burn; Cold applies the Focus Speed reduction; Lightning applies the Focus secondary arc. This is Focus-eligible and can occupy one slot in a Nuke Chain.

source.originalText: Elemental Surge: Channel a concentrated burst of your chosen element, dealing high damage to a single target.

cards.name: Arcane Barrage
cards.effect: Arcane Barrage. Tags: mage-spell, arcanist, arcane, damage. Create S+2 force bolts. Each bolt automatically hits one creature you can perceive within 60 feet for 1d4 force damage. Distribute bolts among any number of legal targets, but all bolts together are one spell cast. This spell is non-elemental and clears an active Nuke Chain.

source.originalText: Arcane Barrage: Launch multiple arcane projectiles that seek out different targets.

cards.name: Metaspell Access
cards.rangeAndTarget: One Mage spell you are beginning to cast
cards.frequency: 1/long rest; choose one metamagic mode when this feature is acquired
cards.effect: Metaspell Access. Tags: arcanist, metamagic. Choose one mode permanently: Reach increases one spell's range by 30 feet; Widen increases one circular radius or cone length by 5 feet; Sculpt lets up to M creatures automatically succeed on that spell's initial area save and take no damage if success normally halves damage. Apply the chosen mode once per long rest before casting; it does not alter RP cost or create another cast.

source.originalText: Metaspell Access: Choose one Universal Metamagic effect to apply to a spell once per day.

cards.name: Conjure Elemental Familiar
cards.effect: Conjure Elemental Familiar. Tags: mage-spell, arcanist, summon, elemental. Summon one elemental familiar matching your current Focus using the common familiar stat block. Only one elemental familiar from this feature may exist at once; summoning another dismisses the first. It obeys the shared Companion Command rule. It disappears at 0 HP or when duration ends and leaves no corpse, XP, loot or resource trigger.

source.originalText: Conjure Elemental Familiar: Summon a minor elemental of your chosen type to assist you in combat.

cards.name: Elemental Mastery
cards.effect: Elemental Mastery. Tags: arcanist, focus. Improve the secondary effect of your current Focus. Fire Burns from your Focus cards last one additional turn but never stack. Cold Focus Speed reductions increase by another 5 feet, minimum 0. Lightning Focus's once-per-turn secondary arc increases from S flat lightning damage to S d4 lightning damage. Pivoted Focus uses the corresponding upgraded rider.

source.originalText: Elemental Mastery: Increase the effectiveness of your chosen element's secondary effects.

cards.name: Displacement
cards.duration: Until start of your next regular turn
cards.effect: Displacement. Tags: mage-spell, arcanist, illusion, teleportation. Teleport up to 20 feet to an unoccupied space you perceive and create two illusory duplicates. Until the start of your next regular turn, the next two attack rolls made against you have disadvantage; each attack roll consumes one duplicate whether it hits or misses. Area effects ignore the duplicates. This non-elemental spell clears an active Nuke Chain.

source.originalText: Displacement: Create illusory duplicates of yourself while teleporting to safety.

cards.name: Counterspell
cards.rangeAndTarget: One creature you perceive casting a spell within 60 feet
cards.effect: Counterspell. Tags: mage-spell, arcanist, disruption. Trigger when a creature begins casting a spell. Make an Intelligence check adding your proficiency bonus against DC 10 + twice the spell's rank, treating rank 0 as 0. On success the triggering spell is negated after its costs are paid. On failure it proceeds normally. Counterspell is non-elemental and, because it is itself a spell, clears an active Nuke Chain.

source.originalText: Counterspell: Disrupt an enemy's spellcasting, potentially negating their spell entirely.

cards.name: Arcane Sanctuary
cards.effect: Arcane Sanctuary. Tags: mage-spell, archmage, zone, concentration. On start and each paid Bonus Action maintenance pulse, allies in the zone gain S+M temporary HP until the start of your next regular turn or effect end, whichever is first and +1 to Mage or spell attack rolls while inside. The zone grants no save-DC increase and no additional Actions. Maximum 3 pulses.

source.originalText: Arcane Sanctuary: Create a zone of protection that shields allies and enhances their magical abilities.

cards.name: Purifying Beam
cards.effect: Purifying Beam. Tags: mage-spell, archmage, radiant, cleansing. Enemies in the line make Dexterity saves, taking (S+1)d8 radiant damage on failure or half on success. Up to M allies in the line may each end one of Charmed, Frightened or Poisoned. Cleansing does not remove Wounds, curses or disease unless another rule expressly allows it. This non-Focus spell clears an active Nuke Chain.

source.originalText: Purifying Beam: Channel a beam of radiant arcane energy that damages enemies and cleanses negative effects from allies.

cards.name: Arcane Bypass
cards.rangeAndTarget: One Mage spell you are beginning to cast
cards.effect: Arcane Bypass. Tags: arcanist, penetration. Before paying costs for a damaging Mage spell, declare Arcane Bypass. Damage from that spell ignores resistance to its printed damage types. Immunity remains immunity. The declaration is spent once the spell is legally cast even if all attacks miss or all targets succeed on saves.

source.originalText: Arcane Bypass: Once per rest, ignore all enemy resistances for one spell.

cards.name: Spell Sharing
cards.cost: 4 RP plus the shared card's printed RP cost
cards.duration: Until end of ally's next regular turn
cards.effect: Spell Sharing. Tags: archmage, spell-sharing. Choose one Base or Arch Mage spell card you know with an Action activation and printed base RP cost 4 or less. Pay both costs now. The ally may cast that card once before the end of its next turn without paying RP, using your Mage spell attack and DC. It cannot share summons, Counterspell, Hero cards, finishers, Resonance Surge or another Spell Sharing.

source.originalText: Spell Sharing: Temporarily grant an ally access to one of your spells.

cards.name: Overload Crits
cards.rangeAndTarget: One enemy within 10 feet of a creature critically hit by your damaging Mage spell
cards.effect: Overload Crits. Tags: arcanist, critical. When a damaging Mage spell scores a critical hit, choose one different enemy within 10 feet of the critically hit target. It takes damage of the same type equal to 50% of the spell's base unmodified damage dice total before critical extra dice, rounded down once, minimum 1. Flat bonuses, riders and critical extra dice are not copied again.

source.originalText: Overload Crits: Critical strikes deal +50% splash damage to nearby enemies.

automaticCards.name: Spellcasting
automaticCards.effect: Spellcasting. Tags: core, spellcasting. You automatically gain Mage spellcasting and access to the Mage repertoire permitted by your separately reconciled spell progression, including Evocation Tier I at the level specified by Core Systems. Use Intelligence for Mage spell attacks and save DCs. This feature is never purchased with a class-feature choice.

source.originalText: Spellcasting: Access to Evocation Tier I spells, focusing on direct damage.

automaticCards.name: Resonance Pool
automaticCards.effect: Resonance Pool. Tags: core, resonance. Your Mage spells and Mage class-spell cards draw from the same Core Systems V 2 Resonance Point pool. Use the authoritative Mage RP maximum by Mage level. This card creates no second pool, no spell slots and no additional recovery method. It is never purchased with a class-feature choice.

source.originalText: Resonance Pool: A reservoir of arcane energy that powers your spells and recovers during rest.

automaticCards.name: Lightning
automaticCards.cost: 0; Storm Arc costs 2 RP when primed
automaticCards.rangeAndTarget: Self; finisher starts on one enemy within 60 feet and may jump twice within 15 feet
automaticCards.frequency: Choose at Mage 2; finisher recharge 3 rounds
automaticCards.effect: Elemental Focus — Lightning. Tags: focus, lightning. Once on each of your turns after a Lightning Mage spell damages a creature, arc S lightning damage to one different enemy within 10 feet. FINISHER — Storm Arc: after a completed Lightning Nuke Chain, Bonus Action, 2 RP. Make separate Mage spell attacks against one enemy within 60 feet and up to two additional different enemies, each within 15 feet of the previous target. Each hit deals S d6 lightning. A target critically hit by Storm Arc makes a Constitution save; failure Stuns it until the end of its next turn.

source.originalText: Lightning: +15% jump chance, arc disruption. Finisher: Storm Arc – Jumps to 3 enemies, stuns on crit

completeEngine: PROVISIONAL PLAYTEST CONTRACT. Intelligence is the Mage class ability. S = 1/2/3/4 at Mage levels 1/5/11/17. M = max(1, Intelligence modifier) unless a feature explicitly says otherwise. Mage spell attack = d20 + normal character proficiency bonus + Intelligence modifier. Mage spell save DC = 8 + normal character proficiency bonus + Intelligence modifier.

Spellcasting and Resonance Pool are automatic class features, never selection taxes. Use the Mage maximum Resonance Point pool and ordinary spell-rank costs from authoritative Core Systems Known Descent V 2. All Mage card RP costs and ordinary spell RP costs come from that same pool. There are no spell slots. A long rest restores RP according to Core V 2; other existing recovery rules remain separate unless this pilot explicitly overrides them.

Named Mage cards tagged mage-spell, and the three Focus finishers are spells for Focus, Nuke Chain, Refrain, concentration, Counterspell and other spell-referencing mechanics. Their printed RP cost replaces an ordinary rank cost; do not charge both. Generic Overcast is disabled for these class-card spells during this pilot unless a card expressly enables it. They receive no extra class-level Burn or Dissonance simply for being card spells; ordinary Core V 2 spell-risk rules still apply where applicable.

Elemental Focus is gained automatically at Mage level 2. Choose Fire, Cold or Lightning and automatically gain the corresponding Focus card. Your selected Focus determines the element used by Elemental Bolt, Elemental Surge, your Focus finisher and other effects that refer to your chosen element. Unless Elemental Pivot or another explicit effect changes it, the choice is permanent in this draft.

NUKE CHAIN. Track your last three consecutive Focus-eligible spell casts. A Focus-eligible cast is a Mage or ordinary spell that deals your currently chosen Fire, Cold or Lightning damage type and is identified by a distinct spell or card name. A spell of another element or a non-elemental spell clears the chain. The last three eligible casts must have three different names. Repeating one chosen-element spell remains a legal cast but shifts the three-cast window and follows ordinary Refrain rules; repetition does not receive special protection from Dissonance.

When the third different named chosen-element spell in the current three-cast window resolves, complete the Nuke Chain, reduce Dissonance by 2 to a minimum of 0, and prime your selected Focus finisher until the end of your next regular Mage turn. Chain completion occurs whether targets hit or save, provided all three spells were legally cast and resolved. A finisher is not itself a chain-building spell. Using the finisher or allowing it to expire clears the chain and the primed state.

FOCUS FINISHERS. A primed Focus finisher is a Bonus Action Mage spell costing 2 RP and is usable once per completed Nuke Chain. Each finisher also has a 3-round recharge. A completed chain can prime a finisher whose recharge is still positive, but the primed use expires normally if the recharge does not become ready in time. Finisher recharge is subject to the universal positive-counter reset limit of once per ability per round.

RESONANCE SURGE. Once per short rest, when you begin casting a damaging Mage spell, you may spend 2 additional RP after validating the spell's normal cost. Add S d8 damage of one damage type already dealt by that spell to one of its damage rolls. Resonance Surge does not count as Overcast, does not independently alter Dissonance or Burn, does not create another spell cast, and does not advance the Nuke Chain separately.

Only one concentration effect may be maintained at a time. Starting another concentration effect ends the first. Damage prompts the current Core Systems concentration save; for this pilot any required half-damage rounding is down. Round recharge counters tick once at the start of your regular initiative turn even if incapacitated, and every uninterrupted 6 seconds outside initiative. Only positive counters may be shortened or reset and each named ability can receive at most one reset or shortening per round.

All sources share a maximum of one additional full Action per creature per round. Additional Actions cannot grant additional Actions, Bonus Actions or Reactions. Mage summons and companions do not receive independent damaging turns: all Mage-controlled conjured companions share one Companion Command per Mage regular turn. Spend one Bonus Action to command exactly one companion to move up to its Speed and use one damaging or control action from its stat block. Uncommanded companions may move to remain near you and take Dodge but cannot deal damage or impose control.

ELEMENTAL FAMILIAR. Conjure Elemental Familiar creates one familiar matching your current Focus; you may have only one elemental familiar. AC = 12 + PB; HP = 5 + Mage level + M; Speed 30 feet; Lightning familiar additionally has Fly 30 feet, Fire has resistance to fire, Cold has resistance to cold. It uses your saves and PB where required. Elemental Dart: ranged spell attack using your Mage spell attack, range 30 feet, hit S d4 damage of its element. It cannot generate RP, Dissonance, Focus casts, corpses, XP, loot or kill-trigger resources.

LICH COMPANION SYSTEM. A successful Lich transformation unlocks three unique bound elite companions: Boneflayer, Dreadblade and Wraithbound. You can maintain at most one of each, maximum three total. They return at full HP after a completed long rest unless a campaign consequence expressly prevents it. A destroyed elite leaves no usable corpse and cannot generate XP, loot, RP, Nuke Chain credit, Soul Reservoir or kill-based resources. Soulbound Ritual can return one before a long rest.

BONEFLAYER. Medium undead; AC 14; HP = 12 + 2 × Mage level; Speed 30 feet. Bone Shards: range 60 feet, your Mage spell attack, hit 2d6 + S necrotic. Fear Pulse: instead of Bone Shards, enemies of your choice within 10 feet make Wisdom saves against your Mage DC; failure causes Frightened until the end of their next turn; recharge 3 rounds. Grave Miasma: instead of Bone Shards, one 10-foot-radius point within 30 feet persists until the start of your next turn; enemies entering or starting there take 1d6 necrotic once; recharge 3 rounds.

DREADBLADE. Medium undead; AC 16; HP = 16 + 3 × Mage level; Speed 30 feet. Disrupting Blade: melee spell attack using your Mage attack bonus, reach 5 feet, hit 1d8 + S necrotic. If the target is concentrating it immediately makes its concentration save with disadvantage. On a natural 20, the target is Weakened until the end of its next turn, taking -1 to attack rolls. Dreadblade has advantage on saves against forced movement.

WRAITHBOUND. Medium undead; AC 14; HP = 10 + 2 × Mage level; Fly 40 feet and can hover. While it has not attacked or imposed control since the end of its previous turn, it is Invisible; attacking ends that state until the end of its next turn. Wraith Strike: melee spell attack using your Mage attack bonus, reach 5 feet, hit 1d8 + S necrotic. On a natural 20, the target makes a Constitution save against your Mage DC; failure Stuns it until the end of its next turn.

LICH TRANSFORMATION READINESS. At Mage level 10 a character may select Lich only after obtaining either one Soul Coin or two ritual participants, binding at least two named mini-bosses as guardians, securing a planar nexus and surviving the Director's divine-echo encounter. A third bound guardian grants +2 to the final ritual check. If both ritual participants are willing, the final ritual check has advantage.

Before the irreversible Lich roll, the Director must explicitly tell the player the historical failure stakes: permanent loss of spellcasting, transformation into a cursed melee undead NPC, hostile faction consequences, cursed-gear restriction and no further XP as that retired PC. The player must explicitly opt into that retirement risk before rolling. If the player declines, the ritual stops before the roll and the character must choose another Hero path for this playtest; no irreversible consequence is applied.

LICH RITUAL CHECK. After all readiness gates and the divine-echo encounter are completed, roll d20 + Intelligence modifier + Constitution modifier against DC 20, applying the third-guardian +2 and willing-participant advantage where applicable. Success completes the Lich transformation and unlocks its cards and elite companions. Failure after explicit consent applies the historical failure state and the Director pauses for the agreed player-to-NPC handoff before continuing play. No silent PC deletion is permitted.

PROPOSED ACQUISITION. Mage 1 automatically gains Spellcasting, Resonance Pool and Resonance Surge, then chooses 4 eligible selectable Base cards, at least 2 Active. Mage 2 automatically chooses and gains one Elemental Focus card, then chooses 2 additional Base cards. Mage 3 enters Arcanist and chooses 2 Arch cards, at least 1 Active. Levels 4 through 9 each grant one eligible unselected Base or Arch card; level 9 is an ordinary choice because the historical source has no Arch capstone.

At Mage 10 choose Archmage, Elementalist or, if its ritual succeeds, Lich; choose 2 cards from that Hero path. Levels 11, 13, 15, 17 and 19 each grant one eligible unselected Base or Arch choice. Levels 12, 14, 16 and 18 each grant one Hero-path choice. Mage 20 grants one additional Hero-path choice plus the NEW playtest level-20 class capstone in extra Cards. No historical Hero Finale is implied. ASI/feat milestones remain separate.

All acquisition gates use Mage class level, not total character level. Proficiency bonus remains the normal total-character proficiency bonus. Non-Mage levels do not unlock Elemental Focus, Arcanist, Hero cards, Nuke Chain upgrades, Lich ritual access or the level-20 Mage capstone.

Class-spell ranks are printed in the normalized card data: use the legal maximum Mage rank at that card's minimum class level, capped 9; the three Focus finishers are rank 1. Rank determines Dissonance, Counterspell and rank-limited interactions, not a second RP cost. A shared spell uses the ally's normal Action and caster-side Dissonance at the moment it is cast; it never builds the Mage's Nuke Chain remotely. Spellcasting through Fracture as Lich uses the shared direct-trauma rule.
mage.automaticAccounting: Arcane Stability+2 applies to Mage concentration damage saves. Lightning Focus/Elemental Affinity cannot improve Cold Ray or Fireball. Those casts/non-elemental Meta clear the chain. No three distinct Lightning casts or finisher. Spell Efficiency and Spell Precision not acquired. Optional Resonance Surge, Arcane Bypass, familiar, Counterspell and Archmage abilities not invoked unless expressly stated.

cards.name: Arcane Recovery
cards.duration: Instantaneous during a completed short rest
cards.effect: Arcane Recovery. Tags: base, passive, resonance. Once between long rests when you complete a short rest, restore RP equal to half your Wizard class level rounded up, never above your normal maximum. This is RP recovery, not a second pool, and cannot trigger spell-cast, Refrain or Dissonance effects.

source.originalText: Arcane Recovery: Once per day during a short rest, recover RP equal to half your Wizard level (rounded up), up to your normal maximum.

cards.name: Spell Scribing
cards.effect: Spell Scribing. Tags: base, passive, spellbook. Copying a legal found Wizard spell into your spellbook requires 1 hour and 25 gp of inks and components per spell rank, treating rank 0 as rank 1 for this calculation, instead of the pilot baseline 2 hours and 50 gp. Level-up spells remain free.

source.originalText: Spell Scribing: Copy spells into your spellbook at half the normal cost and time.

cards.name: Arcane Bolt
cards.effect: Arcane Bolt. Tags: base, active, wizard-spell, universal, damage. Make a Wizard spell attack. On a hit deal S d6 + M force damage. Arcane Bolt is an always-prepared class matrix once acquired and uses the normal first-distinct-matrix and Refrain rules.

source.originalText: Arcane Bolt: Launch a bolt of pure arcane energy that deals force damage to a single target.

cards.name: Minor Conjuration
cards.frequency: At will while RP remains; one object at a time
cards.effect: Minor Conjuration. Tags: base, active, wizard-spell, conjuration. Create one nonmagical unattended object that fits inside a 1-foot cube, weighs no more than 10 pounds and is made of common nonvaluable material such as wood, cloth, clay, iron or glass. It cannot be food, poison, currency, a spell component with listed cost, ammunition with special properties or a functional complex mechanism. Creating another dismisses the first.

source.originalText: Minor Conjuration: Create a temporary, small inanimate object that lasts for 1 hour.

cards.name: Arcane Insight
cards.effect: Arcane Insight. Tags: base, passive, knowledge. Gain proficiency in Arcana, or expertise if already proficient. source.originalText: Arcane Insight: Identify magical effects and items with greater accuracy than non-wizards.

cards.name: Matrix Efficiency
cards.effect: Matrix Efficiency. Tags: base, passive, matrix. Your normal full daily Spell Matrix preparation time is reduced from 1 hour to 45 minutes. This does not reduce the separate 10-minute midday substitution ritual, spell scribing, rituals or spellbook reconstruction unless another feature explicitly says so.

source.originalText: Matrix Efficiency: Reduce the preparation time for spells by 25%.

cards.name: Floating Preparation
cards.effect: Floating Preparation. Tags: arch, passive, matrix. Increase your maximum prepared Spell Matrix count by 1. The extra matrix can come from any school and obeys all ordinary spellbook and rank restrictions. It is a prepared matrix for every rule, including protected strain, duplicate-family tracking and Matrix Mastery modifications.

source.originalText: Floating Preparation: Prepare 1 extra spell from any school each day

cards.name: Arcane Lock
cards.rangeAndTarget: One door, chest, portal or unattended object within touch
cards.effect: Arcane Lock. Tags: arch, active, wizard-spell, abjuration. Magically seal the target. Opening it without your permission requires a Strength check or thieves'/arcane-tool check against your Wizard spell DC. Dispel Magic can end the lock. You can designate up to M creatures who can bypass it. This does not make the object physically indestructible.

source.originalText: Arcane Lock: Create a magical barrier that prevents entry or access to an object or area.

cards.name: Scholarly Mind
cards.effect: Scholarly Mind. Tags: base, passive, knowledge. You have advantage on Intelligence checks whose primary purpose is recalling, researching or analyzing arcane theory, magical history, planar magical principles or constructed spell formulae. It does not grant advantage on spell attacks, Counterspell checks or general Investigation unrelated to arcane scholarship.

source.originalText: Scholarly Mind: Gain advantage on Intelligence checks related to arcane knowledge.

cards.name: Dispel Magic
cards.rangeAndTarget: One creature, object or magical effect within 60 feet
cards.effect: Dispel Magic. Tags: arch, active, wizard-spell, abjuration. Choose one ongoing spell effect you can perceive. If its rank is 3 or lower, end it. If it is rank 4 or higher, make an Intelligence check adding proficiency against DC 10 + spell rank; success ends it. source.originalText: Dispel Magic: End magical effects in an area or on a target.

cards.name: Arcane Sight
cards.effect: Arcane Sight. Tags: arch, active, wizard-spell, divination, concentration. While active you perceive magical auras within 60 feet and automatically know each visible aura's school or broad magical category. As an Action on a later turn, examine one aura to learn whether it is concentrated, summoned, cursed, warded or linked to another visible magical effect. Total cover blocks sight.

source.originalText: Arcane Sight: See magical auras and effects for a short duration.

cards.name: Dimensional Pocket
cards.effect: Dimensional Pocket. Tags: arch, active, wizard-spell, conjuration, ritual. Create an extradimensional storage space holding up to 100 pounds or 10 cubic feet of unattended nonliving material. Retrieving or placing an item while adjacent to the opening uses an object interaction. Living creatures cannot enter. When duration ends, remaining contents appear harmlessly in the nearest unoccupied space.

source.originalText: Dimensional Pocket: Create a small extradimensional space to store items.

cards.name: Analyze Magic
cards.rangeAndTarget: One magical creature, object or effect within 30 feet
cards.effect: Analyze Magic. Tags: base, active, wizard-spell, divination, knowledge. Make an Intelligence (Arcana) check against DC 10 + the effect's spell rank, treating a non-spell effect's Director-assigned tier as rank. On success learn its school or magical category, one active mechanical property and whether it is currently sustained, cursed or bound to another effect. Failure reveals only that magic is present.

source.originalText: Analyze Magic: Study a magical effect or item to gain insight into its properties and function.

cards.name: Sigil Rewrite
cards.effect: Sigil Rewrite. Tags: arch, passive-upgrade, matrix. Replace one prepared matrix with a different spell from your spellbook of exactly the same rank without performing the normal 10-minute ritual. The replacement receives no special Dissonance reset for a matrix family already used this encounter and must obey current Wizard rank eligibility.

source.originalText: Sigil Rewrite: Once/day, instantly swap a spell you know for another of the same tier

cards.name: Spell Preservation
cards.effect: Spell Preservation. Tags: hero, spellbinder, passive, spellbook. Your primary spellbook cannot be destroyed, erased or rendered permanently unreadable by non-artifact mundane or magical means. It can still be stolen, hidden, transported, suppressed, sealed by an artifact-level effect or voluntarily abandoned. Copies and backup books do not automatically receive this protection.

source.originalText: Spell Preservation: Your spellbook cannot be destroyed by non-artifact means.

cards.name: Seal Magic
cards.effect: Seal Magic. Tags: hero, spellbinder, wizard-spell, control. Choose one of the eight schools and target one creature. It makes a Wisdom save. On failure it cannot cast spells of the chosen school. At the end of each of its turns it repeats the save, ending the Seal on success. cards.name: Arcane Shield
cards.duration: Until start of your next regular turn
cards.effect: Arcane Shield. Tags: base, active, wizard-spell, abjuration, protection. Trigger when an attack roll would hit you. cards.rangeAndTarget: Caster whose spell you successfully Counterspelled

cards.name: Spellbook Study
cards.effect: Spellbook Study. Tags: base, active, matrix, ritual. Replace one currently prepared matrix with one legal spell recorded in your spellbook. source.originalText: Spellbook Study: Spend time studying your spellbook to prepare a different selection of spells.

automaticCards.name: Arcane Tradition

automaticCards.effect: Arcane Tradition. Tags: arch, school, automatic. Your level-1 Arcane School becomes your Arcanist tradition; do not choose a second school. Prepare one additional matrix from that same school each day without counting it against your normal prepared-matrix maximum. It otherwise obeys all ordinary rank, spellbook, Dissonance and duplicate-family rules.

source.originalText: Arcane Tradition: Choose a school of magic to specialize in, gaining bonuses to spells of that school.

automaticCards.name: Counterspell

automaticCards.rangeAndTarget: One creature you perceive casting a spell within 60 feet
automaticCards.effect: Counterspell. Tags: arch-source, automatic, wizard-spell, abjuration, disruption. Trigger when a creature begins casting a spell. source.originalText: Counterspell: Disrupt an enemy's spellcasting, potentially negating their spell entirely.

source.originalText: | 5 | Bonus Feat: School Mastery |

automaticCards.name: Arcane Ward
automaticCards.effect: Source progression line 5187. After preparing spells, choose one of acid, cold, fire, force, lightning, necrotic, psychic, radiant or thunder that is dealt by at least one prepared spell of your Arcane School. Gain resistance to that damage type until your next long rest. If none of your prepared school spells deals a damage type, choose force. This is provisional completion of the source's ambiguous 'chosen school's element' wording.

source.originalText: | 6 | Arcane Ward (resistance to chosen school's element) |

automaticCards.name: Dual Cast
automaticCards.cost: Pay the complete RP costs of both spells
automaticCards.effect: Source progression line 5188. Choose two DIFFERENT prepared Wizard spells of rank 1 or 2, neither of which summons a creature or grants an additional Action. Cast both sequentially as one Action, paying both RP costs. They cannot both require concentration. Each matrix separately updates first-cast/Refrain history. Features that trigger merely from 'casting a spell' may trigger once for each actual matrix unless that feature itself says once per turn; no trigger may create another Dual Cast or additional full Action.

automaticCards.cost: Pay the Core V 2 RP cost for one rank above the spell's normal cast rank
automaticCards.rangeAndTarget: One prepared spell you are beginning to cast

Cast one prepared spell as though it were one rank higher than the highest rank at which you could normally cast that SAME spell, provided the spell has an explicit higher-rank scaling rule. Overchannel does not teach or prepare a higher-rank spell, cannot exceed effective rank 9 and cannot be combined with another generic Overcast rule during this pilot. All normal Dissonance/Refrain rules still apply.

completeEngine: PROVISIONAL PLAYTEST CONTRACT. Intelligence is the Wizard class ability. S = 1/2/3/4 at Wizard levels 1/5/11/17. M = max(1, Intelligence modifier). Wizard spell attack = d20 + normal character proficiency bonus + Intelligence modifier. Wizard spell save DC = 8 + normal character proficiency bonus + Intelligence modifier.

The Wizard remains three distinct stages: Base Wizard at levels 1-2, Arch Arcanist at levels 3-9, and one Hero path at levels 10-20: Spellbinder, Elementalist or Necromancer. Hero paths are not additional starting classes and their features cannot be selected before their Wizard class-level gates.

SPELLBOOK. At Wizard 1 your spellbook contains six chosen rank-1 Wizard spells. Arcane School Specialization also adds one legal rank-1 bonus spell of your chosen school without replacing one of those six. For this provisional progression, add 2 legal Wizard spells to the book at each Wizard level 2-4, 3 at each level 5-8, 4 at each level 9-12, 5 at each level 13-16 and 6 at each level 17-20. Level-up additions cost no money or scribing time.

LEGAL RANKS. Maximum Wizard spell rank by Wizard class level is: rank 1 at levels 1-2, rank 2 at 3-4, rank 3 at 5-6, rank 4 at 7-8, rank 5 at 9-10, rank 6 at 11-12, rank 7 at 13-14, rank 8 at 15-16 and rank 9 at 17-20. Grand Tier at level 20 is a special casting permission, not a tenth ordinary rank. A Wizard may learn Wizard-list spells from any school up to the legal rank unless a spell itself has an additional prerequisite.

PREPARED SPELL MATRIX. After a long rest, prepare a number of matrices equal to Wizard level + Intelligence modifier, minimum 1, selecting only spells currently recorded in your spellbook and within your legal rank. You cast ordinary Wizard spells only from prepared matrices unless a feature explicitly overrides that restriction. Preparing the full daily matrix set normally requires 1 hour of spellbook study. Matrix Efficiency reduces this to 45 minutes.

DUPLICATE PREPARATION. You may prepare the same spell more than once, primarily to carry different Matrix Mastery configurations. Duplicate copies never create additional first-cast Dissonance exemptions. For Refrain and the protected strain rule, all prepared copies sharing the same underlying spell name belong to one matrix family regardless of modification.

MIDDAY SUBSTITUTION. Once between long rests, you may perform a 10-minute Spellbook Study ritual to replace one prepared matrix with another legal spell from your spellbook. The replacement cannot exceed your legal Wizard rank. Sigil Rewrite and Matrix Mastery may improve this process as explicitly stated.

SPELL ACQUISITION BY SCRIBING. A found Wizard spell may be copied into the spellbook if its rank is legal for you. Baseline scribing requires 2 hours and 50 gp of inks/materials per spell rank, treating rank 0 as 1 for this calculation. Spell Scribing halves both values to 1 hour and 25 gp per rank. Failure to finish the work consumes no spellbook entry but materials already expended during an interrupted hour are lost.

SPELLBOOK LOSS. Losing the spellbook does not erase matrices currently prepared in memory; you may continue casting those prepared matrices until you next rebuild or change preparation. A blank replacement book can be seeded with your currently prepared spells at 1 hour and 25 gp per effective spell rank each. An unprepared spell you previously recorded can be reconstructed from memory with 8 hours, 100 gp per rank and an Intelligence (Arcana) check against DC 10 + spell rank. Failure consumes that attempt's time and half its materials; another attempt can be made after a long rest. Recovering the original book automatically restores access to its surviving entries.

ARCANE SCHOOL SPECIALIZATION is automatic at Wizard 1. Choose exactly one of the eight schools. Your spell attacks with that school gain +1 and your Wizard save DC for that school's spells gains +1. You also add one legal rank-1 spell of that school to the spellbook. The source table explicitly supplies seven school passives; the eighth core school, Abjuration, is named elsewhere but its passive row is missing. Its provisional playtest passive is identified below rather than silently presented as recovered text.

ABJURATION, provisional completion for the omitted eighth row: once per round after you cast an Abjuration spell, gain temporary HP equal to PB until the start of your next regular turn. CONJURATION: creatures summoned by your Wizard spells gain +1 maximum HP per Wizard level. DIVINATION: once per long rest reroll one failed saving throw and use the new result. ENCHANTMENT: when a creature fails its initial save against one of your Enchantment spells, a printed control duration of at least 1 round may last one additional round, but every normally allowed repeat save still occurs. EVOCATION: when casting an area Evocation spell, exclude one creature from its initial damaging area; that creature automatically succeeds and takes no damage if success normally halves damage. ILLUSION: gain +2 on concentration saves made to maintain Illusion spells. NECROMANCY: once per turn during a real encounter when a hostile non-summoned creature dies from your Necromancy spell, gain 1 temporary HP; it is not permanent healing. TRANSMUTATION: after casting a Transmutation spell, gain +5 feet Speed until the end of that turn.

PROTECTED DISSONANCE INTERFACE. The first cast of each different prepared matrix family during an encounter generates 0 BASE Dissonance. This exemption affects only base strain. Refrain and explicitly printed strain costs still apply; the suite disables generic Overcast and does not layer historical Burn onto Dissonance. Repeating a matrix family follows normal Refrain immediately. Preparing duplicates or differently modified copies of the same underlying spell never refreshes the exemption.

Core Systems V 2 Resonance Points and spell-rank RP costs are authoritative for Wizard spellcasting. There are no historical spell slots in this pilot. Wizard cards tagged wizard-spell are always-prepared class matrices once acquired, do not consume a daily prepared-matrix position and use the same RP, concentration, Refrain and protected first-distinct-matrix rules as other Wizard spells. Their printed RP cost replaces any generic rank cost; never pay both.

RITUAL CASTING is automatic at Wizard 2. A Wizard spell in your spellbook with the Ritual tag can be cast from the book without being prepared by increasing its casting time by at least 10 minutes. A ritual cast costs 0 RP unless that ritual explicitly lists a consumed RP cost, cannot be used during an encounter and cannot generate or vent Dissonance through ordinary casting strain.

Only one concentration effect can normally be maintained. Starting a second concentration effect ends the first. Damage uses the current Core Systems concentration rule; required half-damage rounding is down for this pilot. Spell Tether and the level-17 Tethered Cast are the only Wizard-specific exceptions in this draft, and each has an explicit RP price, duration and one-tether cap.

MATRIX MASTERY MODIFICATIONS. After acquiring Matrix Mastery, each prepared ordinary spell matrix may carry at most one modification chosen during preparation. QUICK SUBSTITUTION: once per short rest, replace one matrix marked Quick Substitution with another spellbook spell of exactly the same rank using a 1-minute ritual instead of the normal 10-minute midday swap; the replacement loses the modification until the next long rest. COMPONENT ENHANCEMENT: when casting a damaging or healing matrix, spend 1 additional RP to add one extra die of the spell's primary damage or healing die to one roll; if the spell has no such die this modification has no effect. MATRIX LINKING: pair two different prepared matrix families during preparation; after legally casting one, the other costs 1 less RP, minimum 1, if cast before the end of your next regular turn, at most once per pair per round. STABILITY REINFORCEMENT: gain +2 on concentration saves caused by damage while maintaining that matrix. A matrix modification never creates another spell cast or proc event.

All sources share a maximum of one additional full Action per creature per round. Additional Actions cannot grant another additional Action, Bonus Action or Reaction. Spell copies, Matrix Sharing, Arcane Fusion, Dual Cast and similar effects pay all explicitly required RP and do not produce duplicate resource, cast-proc or action-grant chains beyond their written resolution.

Round recharge counters decrease once at the start of your regular initiative turn even if you cannot act. Extra Actions and extra turns do not tick recharge. Outside initiative, each uninterrupted 6 seconds counts as one tick. Only positive counters can be reset or shortened and each named ability can receive at most one reset or shortening per round.

SUMMON COMMAND LIMIT. All Wizard-controlled conjured, raised and bound companions share one damaging/control Companion Command per Wizard regular turn. Spend one Bonus Action to command exactly one such creature to move up to its Speed and use one damaging or control action from its stat block. Uncommanded creatures may reposition defensively and take Dodge but cannot deal damage or impose conditions. No summoned or raised creature can create XP, treasure, RP, Dissonance relief, additional corpses or kill-resource farms.

NECROMANCER STANDARD UNDEAD. Corpse Harvest and Auto-Raise share a maximum of three standard raised minions. Skeleton: AC 14, HP 6 + 2 × Wizard level, Speed 30; Bone Shot, range 30 feet, Wizard spell attack, 1d6+S necrotic. Zombie: AC 12, HP 10 + 3 × Wizard level, Speed 20; Slam, reach 5 feet, Wizard spell attack, 1d8+S necrotic. Goblin Thrall, available only from a goblinoid corpse: AC 13, HP 8 + 2 × Wizard level, Speed 30; Shiv, reach 5 feet, Wizard spell attack, 1d6+S necrotic. These are pre-Flesh-Ascendant statistics.

NECROMANCER AUTO-RAISE. Once per round when one of your standard undead minions personally lands the killing blow on an eligible humanoid and your standard-minion count is below three, its corpse rises at the end of the current turn as the same mechanical minion type that scored the kill, if physically possible. A new minion cannot act during that same round. Auto-Raise costs no Action or RP but can never exceed the three-minion cap or generate a new resource, corpse chain, XP or treasure event. Without Infernal Pact only humanoids qualify.

ELITE UNDEAD PETS. Necromancers may bind Boneflayer, Dreadblade and Wraithbound, at most one of each and three elite pets total. They use the same shared Companion Command limit as standard undead. Boneflayer: AC 14, HP 12 + 2 × Wizard level, Speed 30. Bone Shards: range 60, Wizard spell attack, 2d6+S necrotic. Fear Pulse replaces its attack: enemies within 10 feet make Wisdom saves; failure Frightened until end of next turn; recharge 3. Grave Miasma replaces its attack: 10-foot-radius point within 30 feet until start of your next turn; enemies entering or starting there take 1d6 necrotic once; recharge 3.

Dreadblade: AC 16, HP 16 + 3 × Wizard level, Speed 30. Disrupting Blade: reach 5 feet, Wizard spell attack, 1d8+S necrotic; a concentrating target immediately makes its concentration save with disadvantage. On a natural 20 the target is Weakened until the end of its next turn, taking -1 on attack rolls. Dreadblade has advantage on saves against forced movement.

Wraithbound: AC 14, HP 10 + 2 × Wizard level, Fly 40 and hover. While it has not attacked or imposed control since the end of its previous turn it is Invisible; attacking ends that state until the end of its next turn. Wraith Strike: reach 5 feet, Wizard spell attack, 1d8+S necrotic. On natural 20 the target makes a Constitution save against your Wizard DC; failure Stuns until the end of its next turn.

Flesh Ascendant's bonus applies after the listed base statistics: every undead creature you control gains +2 maximum HP per Wizard level. If at least two of your undead creatures are active, each gains +1 AC and +1 on saving throws. This does not increase the standard-minion or elite-pet caps.

DARK-TRAUMA INTERFACE. Necromancer features involving corpse desecration, infernal bargains, domination, body control or Mind Prison remain subject to the project's existing dark-content and trauma boundaries. A table may fade description to black without changing mechanics. No feature changes a player's real belief, permanently transfers ownership of a player character or silently retires a PC.

PROPOSED ACQUISITION. Wizard 1 automatically gains Arcane School Specialization, Spell Matrix System and the starting spellbook, then chooses 4 selectable Base cards, at least 2 Active. Wizard 2 automatically gains Counterspell and Ritual Casting, then chooses 2 additional selectable Base cards. Counterspell is not also placed in the Arch selection pool.

At Wizard 3 enter Arcanist, automatically gain Arcane Tradition as an upgrade of the SAME level-1 school rather than choosing another school, and choose 2 selectable Arch cards, at least 1 Active. Wizard 4 grants one eligible Base/Arch choice. Wizard 5 grants one Base/Arch choice plus automatic School Mastery. Wizard 6 grants one Base/Arch choice plus automatic Arcane Ward. Wizard 7 grants one eligible Arch choice. Wizard 8 grants one Base/Arch choice. Wizard 9 grants one eligible Arch choice plus automatic Dual Cast.

At Wizard 10 choose Spellbinder, Elementalist or Necromancer and gain 2 Hero cards from that path. ELEMENTALIST EXCEPTION: Elemental Affinity is automatic at path selection and counts as one of those two level-10 Hero acquisitions, so an Elementalist chooses only one additional Hero card at level 10. Levels 11, 13, 15, 17 and 19 each grant one eligible unselected Base/Arch choice. Levels 12, 14, 16 and 18 each grant one Hero-path choice. The chosen Final Theorem is automatic at Wizard 20. School Mastery, Counterspell, Arcane Tradition and all progression-table automatic features are never duplicated as selections.

All acquisition gates use Wizard class level rather than total character level. Normal proficiency bonus follows the game's ordinary total-character-level rule. A multiclass dip cannot unlock higher spell ranks, Arcanist cards, Hero cards, Final Theorems or progression-table features.

Class matrices tagged wizard-spell receive a rank in normalized card data equal to maximum ordinary Wizard rank at their minimum class-level gate (cap 9). Printed RP cost replaces generic rank cost. Counterspell is rank 1 at its explicit level 2 automatic grant. This explicit convention closes rank-dependent Counterspell/Dissonance interactions without inventing extra costs.

Cantrip completion: know 3 Wizard cantrips at 1, 4 at 4, 5 at 10, using the shared missing-repertoire fallback. Cantrips are known directly and do not consume prepared matrices. Always-prepared class matrices are additional cards, not extra arbitrary ordinary spells. Class spell ranks and the normalized activation field resolve incomplete source terminology.
target.optionalChoicesInCases: No Matrix Mastery, Spell Efficiency, Improved Concentration, Sigil Authority or Knowledge Shield acquired. Dual Cast, Overchannel, class Arcane Shield and optional Counterpulse are not invoked unless expressly declared. No Arcane Feedback at13.
target.profileScope: An explicitly supplied finite class-built teaching creature profile using the complete actual class engine/cards. Not a newly rated bestiary creature, not authenticated campaign or ancestry acquisition, and not permission to fill an absent future profile.

cards.name: Arcane Recovery
cards.duration: Instantaneous during a completed short rest
cards.effect: Arcane Recovery. Tags: base, passive, resonance. Once between long rests when you complete a short rest, restore RP equal to half your Wizard class level rounded up, never above your normal maximum. This is RP recovery, not a second pool, and cannot trigger spell-cast, Refrain or Dissonance effects.

source.originalText: Arcane Recovery: Once per day during a short rest, recover RP equal to half your Wizard level (rounded up), up to your normal maximum.

cards.name: Spell Scribing
cards.effect: Spell Scribing. Tags: base, passive, spellbook. Copying a legal found Wizard spell into your spellbook requires 1 hour and 25 gp of inks and components per spell rank, treating rank 0 as rank 1 for this calculation, instead of the pilot baseline 2 hours and 50 gp. Level-up spells remain free.

source.originalText: Spell Scribing: Copy spells into your spellbook at half the normal cost and time.

cards.name: Arcane Bolt
cards.effect: Arcane Bolt. Tags: base, active, wizard-spell, universal, damage. Make a Wizard spell attack. On a hit deal S d6 + M force damage. Arcane Bolt is an always-prepared class matrix once acquired and uses the normal first-distinct-matrix and Refrain rules.

source.originalText: Arcane Bolt: Launch a bolt of pure arcane energy that deals force damage to a single target.

cards.name: Minor Conjuration
cards.frequency: At will while RP remains; one object at a time
cards.effect: Minor Conjuration. Tags: base, active, wizard-spell, conjuration. Create one nonmagical unattended object that fits inside a 1-foot cube, weighs no more than 10 pounds and is made of common nonvaluable material such as wood, cloth, clay, iron or glass. It cannot be food, poison, currency, a spell component with listed cost, ammunition with special properties or a functional complex mechanism. Creating another dismisses the first.

source.originalText: Minor Conjuration: Create a temporary, small inanimate object that lasts for 1 hour.

cards.name: Arcane Insight
cards.effect: Arcane Insight. Tags: base, passive, knowledge. Gain proficiency in Arcana, or expertise if already proficient. When examining an active magical effect, spell residue, magic item or arcane construction, you may make an Intelligence (Arcana) check to determine its broad school, function or unusual matrix behavior. The Director sets the normal knowledge DC; failure supplies no invented fact.

source.originalText: Arcane Insight: Identify magical effects and items with greater accuracy than non-wizards.

cards.name: Matrix Efficiency
cards.effect: Matrix Efficiency. Tags: base, passive, matrix. Your normal full daily Spell Matrix preparation time is reduced from 1 hour to 45 minutes. This does not reduce the separate 10-minute midday substitution ritual, spell scribing, rituals or spellbook reconstruction unless another feature explicitly says so.

source.originalText: Matrix Efficiency: Reduce the preparation time for spells by 25%.

cards.name: Floating Preparation
cards.effect: Floating Preparation. Tags: arch, passive, matrix. Increase your maximum prepared Spell Matrix count by 1. The extra matrix can come from any school and obeys all ordinary spellbook and rank restrictions. It is a prepared matrix for every rule, including protected strain, duplicate-family tracking and Matrix Mastery modifications.

source.originalText: Floating Preparation: Prepare 1 extra spell from any school each day

cards.name: Arcane Lock
cards.rangeAndTarget: One door, chest, portal or unattended object within touch
cards.effect: Arcane Lock. Tags: arch, active, wizard-spell, abjuration. Magically seal the target. Opening it without your permission requires a Strength check or thieves'/arcane-tool check against your Wizard spell DC. Dispel Magic can end the lock. You can designate up to M creatures who can bypass it. This does not make the object physically indestructible.

source.originalText: Arcane Lock: Create a magical barrier that prevents entry or access to an object or area.

cards.name: Scholarly Mind
cards.effect: Scholarly Mind. Tags: base, passive, knowledge. You have advantage on Intelligence checks whose primary purpose is recalling, researching or analyzing arcane theory, magical history, planar magical principles or constructed spell formulae. It does not grant advantage on spell attacks, Counterspell checks or general Investigation unrelated to arcane scholarship.

source.originalText: Scholarly Mind: Gain advantage on Intelligence checks related to arcane knowledge.

cards.name: Dispel Magic
cards.rangeAndTarget: One creature, object or magical effect within 60 feet
cards.effect: Dispel Magic. Tags: arch, active, wizard-spell, abjuration. Choose one ongoing spell effect you can perceive. If its rank is 3 or lower, end it. If it is rank 4 or higher, make an Intelligence check adding proficiency against DC 10 + spell rank; success ends it. Permanent artifact properties and effects explicitly immune to dispelling are unaffected.

source.originalText: Dispel Magic: End magical effects in an area or on a target.

cards.name: Arcane Sight
cards.effect: Arcane Sight. Tags: arch, active, wizard-spell, divination, concentration. While active you perceive magical auras within 60 feet and automatically know each visible aura's school or broad magical category. As an Action on a later turn, examine one aura to learn whether it is concentrated, summoned, cursed, warded or linked to another visible magical effect. Total cover blocks sight.

source.originalText: Arcane Sight: See magical auras and effects for a short duration.

cards.name: Dimensional Pocket
cards.effect: Dimensional Pocket. Tags: arch, active, wizard-spell, conjuration, ritual. Create an extradimensional storage space holding up to 100 pounds or 10 cubic feet of unattended nonliving material. Retrieving or placing an item while adjacent to the opening uses an object interaction. Living creatures cannot enter. When duration ends, remaining contents appear harmlessly in the nearest unoccupied space.

source.originalText: Dimensional Pocket: Create a small extradimensional space to store items.

cards.name: Analyze Magic
cards.rangeAndTarget: One magical creature, object or effect within 30 feet
cards.effect: Analyze Magic. Tags: base, active, wizard-spell, divination, knowledge. Make an Intelligence (Arcana) check against DC 10 + the effect's spell rank, treating a non-spell effect's Director-assigned tier as rank. On success learn its school or magical category, one active mechanical property and whether it is currently sustained, cursed or bound to another effect. Failure reveals only that magic is present.

source.originalText: Analyze Magic: Study a magical effect or item to gain insight into its properties and function.

cards.name: Sigil Rewrite
cards.effect: Sigil Rewrite. Tags: arch, passive-upgrade, matrix. Replace one prepared matrix with a different spell from your spellbook of exactly the same rank without performing the normal 10-minute ritual. The replacement receives no special Dissonance reset for a matrix family already used this encounter and must obey current Wizard rank eligibility.

source.originalText: Sigil Rewrite: Once/day, instantly swap a spell you know for another of the same tier

cards.name: Spell Preservation
cards.effect: Spell Preservation. Tags: hero, spellbinder, passive, spellbook. Your primary spellbook cannot be destroyed, erased or rendered permanently unreadable by non-artifact mundane or magical means. It can still be stolen, hidden, transported, suppressed, sealed by an artifact-level effect or voluntarily abandoned. Copies and backup books do not automatically receive this protection.

source.originalText: Spell Preservation: Your spellbook cannot be destroyed by non-artifact means.

cards.name: Seal Magic
cards.effect: Seal Magic. Tags: hero, spellbinder, wizard-spell, control. Choose one of the eight schools and target one creature. It makes a Wisdom save. On failure it cannot cast spells of the chosen school. At the end of each of its turns it repeats the save, ending the Seal on success. The effect ends automatically after 3 rounds and never prevents non-spell class techniques merely because they are magical.

source.originalText: Seal Magic: Prevent a target from casting spells of a specific school (WIS save, 3 rounds)

cards.name: Arcane Shield
cards.duration: Until start of your next regular turn
cards.effect: Arcane Shield. Tags: base, active, wizard-spell, abjuration, protection. Trigger when an attack roll would hit you. Gain +2 AC against the triggering attack and until the start of your next regular turn, potentially causing the attack to miss. Temporary AC from another Arcane Shield does not stack.

source.originalText: Arcane Shield: Create a barrier of magical force that provides temporary protection.

cards.name: Counterpulse
cards.rangeAndTarget: Caster whose spell you successfully Counterspelled
cards.duration: Until end of target's next turn
cards.effect: Counterpulse. Tags: hero, spellbinder, counter, control. Immediately after your Counterspell succeeds, spend 1 RP. The countered caster is Silenced until the end of its next turn. source.originalText: Counterpulse: Countering a spell silences the caster for 1 round

cards.name: Spellbook Study
cards.effect: Spellbook Study. Tags: base, active, matrix, ritual. Replace one currently prepared matrix with one legal spell recorded in your spellbook. The replacement must be within your Wizard rank limit. This is the normal midday substitution permission; it does not alter the spellbook, create another prepared-matrix position or reset first-cast/Refrain history for an underlying matrix family already cast this encounter.

source.originalText: Spellbook Study: Spend time studying your spellbook to prepare a different selection of spells.

source.originalText: Arcane Tradition: Choose a school of magic to specialize in, gaining bonuses to spells of that school.

automaticCards.effect: Counterspell. Tags: arch-source, automatic, wizard-spell, abjuration, disruption. Trigger when a creature begins casting a spell. automaticCards.cost: Pay the complete RP costs of both spells
automaticCards.effect: Source progression line 5188. Choose two DIFFERENT prepared Wizard spells of rank 1 or 2, neither of which summons a creature or grants an additional Action. automaticCards.cost: Pay the Core V 2 RP cost for one rank above the spell's normal cast rank

completeEngine: PROVISIONAL PLAYTEST CONTRACT. Intelligence is the Wizard class ability. S = 1/2/3/4 at Wizard levels 1/5/11/17. M = max(1, Intelligence modifier). Wizard spell attack = d20 + normal character proficiency bonus + Intelligence modifier. Wizard spell save DC = 8 + normal character proficiency bonus + Intelligence modifier.

The Wizard remains three distinct stages: Base Wizard at levels 1-2, Arch Arcanist at levels 3-9, and one Hero path at levels 10-20: Spellbinder, Elementalist or Necromancer. Hero paths are not additional starting classes and their features cannot be selected before their Wizard class-level gates.

SPELLBOOK. At Wizard 1 your spellbook contains six chosen rank-1 Wizard spells. Arcane School Specialization also adds one legal rank-1 bonus spell of your chosen school without replacing one of those six. For this provisional progression, add 2 legal Wizard spells to the book at each Wizard level 2-4, 3 at each level 5-8, 4 at each level 9-12, 5 at each level 13-16 and 6 at each level 17-20. Level-up additions cost no money or scribing time.

LEGAL RANKS. Maximum Wizard spell rank by Wizard class level is: rank 1 at levels 1-2, rank 2 at 3-4, rank 3 at 5-6, rank 4 at 7-8, rank 5 at 9-10, rank 6 at 11-12, rank 7 at 13-14, rank 8 at 15-16 and rank 9 at 17-20. Grand Tier at level 20 is a special casting permission, not a tenth ordinary rank. A Wizard may learn Wizard-list spells from any school up to the legal rank unless a spell itself has an additional prerequisite.

PREPARED SPELL MATRIX. After a long rest, prepare a number of matrices equal to Wizard level + Intelligence modifier, minimum 1, selecting only spells currently recorded in your spellbook and within your legal rank. You cast ordinary Wizard spells only from prepared matrices unless a feature explicitly overrides that restriction. Preparing the full daily matrix set normally requires 1 hour of spellbook study. Matrix Efficiency reduces this to 45 minutes.

DUPLICATE PREPARATION. You may prepare the same spell more than once, primarily to carry different Matrix Mastery configurations. Duplicate copies never create additional first-cast Dissonance exemptions. For Refrain and the protected strain rule, all prepared copies sharing the same underlying spell name belong to one matrix family regardless of modification.

MIDDAY SUBSTITUTION. Once between long rests, you may perform a 10-minute Spellbook Study ritual to replace one prepared matrix with another legal spell from your spellbook. The replacement cannot exceed your legal Wizard rank. Sigil Rewrite and Matrix Mastery may improve this process as explicitly stated.

SPELL ACQUISITION BY SCRIBING. A found Wizard spell may be copied into the spellbook if its rank is legal for you. Baseline scribing requires 2 hours and 50 gp of inks/materials per spell rank, treating rank 0 as 1 for this calculation. Spell Scribing halves both values to 1 hour and 25 gp per rank. Failure to finish the work consumes no spellbook entry but materials already expended during an interrupted hour are lost.

SPELLBOOK LOSS. Losing the spellbook does not erase matrices currently prepared in memory; you may continue casting those prepared matrices until you next rebuild or change preparation. A blank replacement book can be seeded with your currently prepared spells at 1 hour and 25 gp per effective spell rank each. An unprepared spell you previously recorded can be reconstructed from memory with 8 hours, 100 gp per rank and an Intelligence (Arcana) check against DC 10 + spell rank. Failure consumes that attempt's time and half its materials; another attempt can be made after a long rest. Recovering the original book automatically restores access to its surviving entries.

ARCANE SCHOOL SPECIALIZATION is automatic at Wizard 1. Choose exactly one of the eight schools. Your spell attacks with that school gain +1 and your Wizard save DC for that school's spells gains +1. You also add one legal rank-1 spell of that school to the spellbook. The source table explicitly supplies seven school passives; the eighth core school, Abjuration, is named elsewhere but its passive row is missing. Its provisional playtest passive is identified below rather than silently presented as recovered text.

ABJURATION, provisional completion for the omitted eighth row: once per round after you cast an Abjuration spell, gain temporary HP equal to PB until the start of your next regular turn. CONJURATION: creatures summoned by your Wizard spells gain +1 maximum HP per Wizard level. DIVINATION: once per long rest reroll one failed saving throw and use the new result. ENCHANTMENT: when a creature fails its initial save against one of your Enchantment spells, a printed control duration of at least 1 round may last one additional round, but every normally allowed repeat save still occurs. EVOCATION: when casting an area Evocation spell, exclude one creature from its initial damaging area; that creature automatically succeeds and takes no damage if success normally halves damage. ILLUSION: gain +2 on concentration saves made to maintain Illusion spells. NECROMANCY: once per turn during a real encounter when a hostile non-summoned creature dies from your Necromancy spell, gain 1 temporary HP; it is not permanent healing. TRANSMUTATION: after casting a Transmutation spell, gain +5 feet Speed until the end of that turn.

PROTECTED DISSONANCE INTERFACE. The first cast of each different prepared matrix family during an encounter generates 0 BASE Dissonance. This exemption affects only base strain. Refrain and explicitly printed strain costs still apply; the suite disables generic Overcast and does not layer historical Burn onto Dissonance. Repeating a matrix family follows normal Refrain immediately. Preparing duplicates or differently modified copies of the same underlying spell never refreshes the exemption.

Core Systems V 2 Resonance Points and spell-rank RP costs are authoritative for Wizard spellcasting. There are no historical spell slots in this pilot. Wizard cards tagged wizard-spell are always-prepared class matrices once acquired, do not consume a daily prepared-matrix position and use the same RP, concentration, Refrain and protected first-distinct-matrix rules as other Wizard spells. Their printed RP cost replaces any generic rank cost; never pay both.

RITUAL CASTING is automatic at Wizard 2. A Wizard spell in your spellbook with the Ritual tag can be cast from the book without being prepared by increasing its casting time by at least 10 minutes. A ritual cast costs 0 RP unless that ritual explicitly lists a consumed RP cost, cannot be used during an encounter and cannot generate or vent Dissonance through ordinary casting strain.

Only one concentration effect can normally be maintained. Starting a second concentration effect ends the first. Damage uses the current Core Systems concentration rule; required half-damage rounding is down for this pilot. Spell Tether and the level-17 Tethered Cast are the only Wizard-specific exceptions in this draft, and each has an explicit RP price, duration and one-tether cap.

MATRIX MASTERY MODIFICATIONS. After acquiring Matrix Mastery, each prepared ordinary spell matrix may carry at most one modification chosen during preparation. QUICK SUBSTITUTION: once per short rest, replace one matrix marked Quick Substitution with another spellbook spell of exactly the same rank using a 1-minute ritual instead of the normal 10-minute midday swap; the replacement loses the modification until the next long rest. COMPONENT ENHANCEMENT: when casting a damaging or healing matrix, spend 1 additional RP to add one extra die of the spell's primary damage or healing die to one roll; if the spell has no such die this modification has no effect. MATRIX LINKING: pair two different prepared matrix families during preparation; after legally casting one, the other costs 1 less RP, minimum 1, if cast before the end of your next regular turn, at most once per pair per round. STABILITY REINFORCEMENT: gain +2 on concentration saves caused by damage while maintaining that matrix. A matrix modification never creates another spell cast or proc event.

All sources share a maximum of one additional full Action per creature per round. Additional Actions cannot grant another additional Action, Bonus Action or Reaction. Spell copies, Matrix Sharing, Arcane Fusion, Dual Cast and similar effects pay all explicitly required RP and do not produce duplicate resource, cast-proc or action-grant chains beyond their written resolution.

Round recharge counters decrease once at the start of your regular initiative turn even if you cannot act. Extra Actions and extra turns do not tick recharge. Outside initiative, each uninterrupted 6 seconds counts as one tick. Only positive counters can be reset or shortened and each named ability can receive at most one reset or shortening per round.

SUMMON COMMAND LIMIT. All Wizard-controlled conjured, raised and bound companions share one damaging/control Companion Command per Wizard regular turn. Spend one Bonus Action to command exactly one such creature to move up to its Speed and use one damaging or control action from its stat block. Uncommanded creatures may reposition defensively and take Dodge but cannot deal damage or impose conditions. No summoned or raised creature can create XP, treasure, RP, Dissonance relief, additional corpses or kill-resource farms.

NECROMANCER STANDARD UNDEAD. Corpse Harvest and Auto-Raise share a maximum of three standard raised minions. Skeleton: AC 14, HP 6 + 2 × Wizard level, Speed 30; Bone Shot, range 30 feet, Wizard spell attack, 1d6+S necrotic. Zombie: AC 12, HP 10 + 3 × Wizard level, Speed 20; Slam, reach 5 feet, Wizard spell attack, 1d8+S necrotic. Goblin Thrall, available only from a goblinoid corpse: AC 13, HP 8 + 2 × Wizard level, Speed 30; Shiv, reach 5 feet, Wizard spell attack, 1d6+S necrotic. These are pre-Flesh-Ascendant statistics.

NECROMANCER AUTO-RAISE. Once per round when one of your standard undead minions personally lands the killing blow on an eligible humanoid and your standard-minion count is below three, its corpse rises at the end of the current turn as the same mechanical minion type that scored the kill, if physically possible. A new minion cannot act during that same round. Auto-Raise costs no Action or RP but can never exceed the three-minion cap or generate a new resource, corpse chain, XP or treasure event. Without Infernal Pact only humanoids qualify.

ELITE UNDEAD PETS. Necromancers may bind Boneflayer, Dreadblade and Wraithbound, at most one of each and three elite pets total. They use the same shared Companion Command limit as standard undead. Boneflayer: AC 14, HP 12 + 2 × Wizard level, Speed 30. Bone Shards: range 60, Wizard spell attack, 2d6+S necrotic. Fear Pulse replaces its attack: enemies within 10 feet make Wisdom saves; failure Frightened until end of next turn; recharge 3. Grave Miasma replaces its attack: 10-foot-radius point within 30 feet until start of your next turn; enemies entering or starting there take 1d6 necrotic once; recharge 3.

Dreadblade: AC 16, HP 16 + 3 × Wizard level, Speed 30. Disrupting Blade: reach 5 feet, Wizard spell attack, 1d8+S necrotic; a concentrating target immediately makes its concentration save with disadvantage. On a natural 20 the target is Weakened until the end of its next turn, taking -1 on attack rolls. Dreadblade has advantage on saves against forced movement.

Wraithbound: AC 14, HP 10 + 2 × Wizard level, Fly 40 and hover. While it has not attacked or imposed control since the end of its previous turn it is Invisible; attacking ends that state until the end of its next turn. Wraith Strike: reach 5 feet, Wizard spell attack, 1d8+S necrotic. On natural 20 the target makes a Constitution save against your Wizard DC; failure Stuns until the end of its next turn.

Flesh Ascendant's bonus applies after the listed base statistics: every undead creature you control gains +2 maximum HP per Wizard level. If at least two of your undead creatures are active, each gains +1 AC and +1 on saving throws. This does not increase the standard-minion or elite-pet caps.

DARK-TRAUMA INTERFACE. Necromancer features involving corpse desecration, infernal bargains, domination, body control or Mind Prison remain subject to the project's existing dark-content and trauma boundaries. A table may fade description to black without changing mechanics. No feature changes a player's real belief, permanently transfers ownership of a player character or silently retires a PC.

PROPOSED ACQUISITION. Wizard 1 automatically gains Arcane School Specialization, Spell Matrix System and the starting spellbook, then chooses 4 selectable Base cards, at least 2 Active. Wizard 2 automatically gains Counterspell and Ritual Casting, then chooses 2 additional selectable Base cards. Counterspell is not also placed in the Arch selection pool.

At Wizard 3 enter Arcanist, automatically gain Arcane Tradition as an upgrade of the SAME level-1 school rather than choosing another school, and choose 2 selectable Arch cards, at least 1 Active. Wizard 4 grants one eligible Base/Arch choice. Wizard 5 grants one Base/Arch choice plus automatic School Mastery. Wizard 6 grants one Base/Arch choice plus automatic Arcane Ward. Wizard 7 grants one eligible Arch choice. Wizard 8 grants one Base/Arch choice. Wizard 9 grants one eligible Arch choice plus automatic Dual Cast.

At Wizard 10 choose Spellbinder, Elementalist or Necromancer and gain 2 Hero cards from that path. ELEMENTALIST EXCEPTION: Elemental Affinity is automatic at path selection and counts as one of those two level-10 Hero acquisitions, so an Elementalist chooses only one additional Hero card at level 10. Levels 11, 13, 15, 17 and 19 each grant one eligible unselected Base/Arch choice. Levels 12, 14, 16 and 18 each grant one Hero-path choice. The chosen Final Theorem is automatic at Wizard 20. School Mastery, Counterspell, Arcane Tradition and all progression-table automatic features are never duplicated as selections.

All acquisition gates use Wizard class level rather than total character level. Normal proficiency bonus follows the game's ordinary total-character-level rule. A multiclass dip cannot unlock higher spell ranks, Arcanist cards, Hero cards, Final Theorems or progression-table features.

Class matrices tagged wizard-spell receive a rank in normalized card data equal to maximum ordinary Wizard rank at their minimum class-level gate (cap 9). Printed RP cost replaces generic rank cost. Counterspell is rank 1 at its explicit level 2 automatic grant. This explicit convention closes rank-dependent Counterspell/Dissonance interactions without inventing extra costs.

Cantrip completion: know 3 Wizard cantrips at 1, 4 at 4, 5 at 10, using the shared missing-repertoire fallback. Cantrips are known directly and do not consume prepared matrices. Always-prepared class matrices are additional cards, not extra arbitrary ordinary spells. Class spell ranks and the normalized activation field resolve incomplete source terminology.

cards.name: Arcane Insight

After examining a magical item, spell residue, ward or active magical effect for 1 minute, you may make an Intelligence (Arcana) check to identify its school, broad function or elemental signature. The Director sets the normal knowledge DC; failure supplies no fabricated information.

source.originalText: Arcane Insight: Identify magical effects and items with greater accuracy than non-mages.

cards.name: Arcane Missile
cards.effect: Arcane Missile. Tags: mage-spell, arcane, damage. The missile automatically hits one creature you can perceive within range and deals S d4 + M force damage. No attack roll or saving throw is made. It is non-elemental, so casting it clears an Elemental Focus Nuke Chain. Multiple missiles are represented by the scaling dice, not separate hits or triggers.

source.originalText: Arcane Missile: Launch bolts of pure arcane energy that unerringly strike your target.

cards.name: Resonance Shield
cards.cost: Spend X RP, where X is 1, 2 or 3
cards.duration: 1 minute or until temporary HP are lost
cards.effect: Resonance Shield. Tags: mage-spell, abjuration, protection. Spend 1-3 RP and gain temporary HP equal to X × (S + M). Temporary HP do not stack. source.originalText: Resonance Shield: Convert a portion of your Resonance Points into a temporary protective barrier.

cards.name: Blink
cards.effect: Blink. Tags: mage-spell, teleportation. Teleport to an unoccupied space you can perceive within 30 feet. This movement does not provoke opportunity attacks and cannot pass through planar wards that prohibit teleportation. source.originalText: Blink: Teleport a short distance to avoid danger or reposition.

cards.name: Elemental Affinity
